text_block_list.name: Mejiro Palmer
text_block_list.text: Ardenn-sa~~n!! Help us!!

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Ardenn
text_block_list.text:
Oh my, Palmer and Helios-san. Fufu... do 
you have another exam coming up?

text_block_list.name: Daitaku Helios
text_block_list.text:
Yup! On the Edo period, I think? We got 
another test coming up, and it's mega 
insane demon-mode hard~! Ardenn-senpai, 
please teach us~~!!

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Ardenn
text_block_list.text:
The Edo period, is it... Then, since we 
have the opportunity, let us learn 
enjoyably through hands-on experience♪

text_block_list.name: Both
text_block_list.text: ...Huh?

text_block_list.name: Both
text_block_list.text: ...Why a hot spring?

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Ardenn
text_block_list.text:
Fufu, the hot spring is not our primary 
purpose today. In fact, this inn was 
founded in the Edo period, and they hold 
workshops for traditional crafts here.

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Ardenn
text_block_list.text:
This is a rare opportunity to directly 
experience the history and culture of the 
Edo period through hands-on practice. 
Shall we learn while crafting here today?

text_block_list.name: Daitaku Helios
text_block_list.text:
Founded in the Edo era? That's mad 
emotional vibes! Hype levels maxed, let's 
goooo~!

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Palmer
text_block_list.text:
A hands-on workshop sounds super fun too! 
I'm in, I'm totally in~!

text_block_list.name: Inn Staff
text_block_list.text:
The craft technique known as "tsumami 
zaiku", established during the Edo period, 
became immensely popular. Today, let us 
try making a kanzashi hairpin using this 
technique.

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Palmer
text_block_list.text:
Phew~~...! Detailed work like this is 
tough!

text_block_list.name: Daitaku Helios
text_block_list.text:
I'm barely getting anywhere either! Wait 
wait, isn't this "tsumami zaiku" thing 
seriously insane technique?

text_block_list.name: Daitaku Helios
text_block_list.text:
Making gorge flowers out of such tiny, 
finicky folding, and sticking that in your 
hair? That is mega emotional vibes!

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Ardenn
text_block_list.text:
Fufu, the people of the Edo period truly 
lived those very "mega emotional" lives. 
Shall we try imagining it—?

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Ardenn
text_block_list.text:
The Edo period was also the era when 
kabuki, as handed down today, flourished. 
Kabuki actors were treated like superstars 
among the common folk—

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Ardenn
text_block_list.text:
Fashion trends in the town of Edo were 
driven by kabuki actors. From how kimonos 
were worn to the kanzashi hairpins chosen, 
everyone scrambled to copy them.

text_block_list.name: Daitaku Helios
text_block_list.text:
For real!? That's just like modern models 
and idols!

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Palmer
text_block_list.text:
Dressing up cute with fancy hairpins~ and 
stanning kabuki actors? That sounds so 
fun!

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Ardenn
text_block_list.text:
Yes. Wearing kimono with trendy checkered 
patterns, tying their obi sash to imitate 
their favorite kabuki actor, and eagerly 
collecting ukiyo-e woodblock prints of 
them.

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Palmer
text_block_list.text:
Like stan culture, right? I can totally 
get wanting to copy your fave!

text_block_list.name: Daitaku Helios
text_block_list.text:
Wait wait, the trend in Edo was plaid 
patterns!? That's beyond cute! I wanna 
wear blue plaid too~!

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Ardenn
text_block_list.text:
Street stalls selling soba noodles were 
also an enormous craze in Edo. Perhaps 
they even stood in long lines waiting for 
their turn... Just like today, wouldn't 
you say?

text_block_list.name: Daitaku Helios
text_block_list.text:
Like queuing up for pancakes at trendy 
cafes now? Ahaha, what they were doing is 
literally the exact same as us!

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Ardenn
text_block_list.text:
The Edo period lasted for over 260 years, 
and governance was relatively peaceful and 
stable, which is why townsperson culture 
flourished so magnificently.

text_block_list.name: Daitaku Helios
text_block_list.text:
Huh~... So does that mean the feudal lords 
were super awesome and nice people?

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Ardenn
text_block_list.text:
Yes. Because the political framework was 
solidly established, there were capable 
officials supporting the lord—the supreme 
Shogun. That is why the governance 
remained so stable.

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Palmer
text_block_list.text:
I see, I see! So that means... uh, the 
first shogun of the Edo period was Ieyasu, 
right? That guy totally birthed an 
incredible system!

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Palmer
text_block_list.text:
Man, that was so fun and informative! I 
totally get the Edo period now!

text_block_list.name: Daitaku Helios
text_block_list.text:
For real! Ardan-senpai, you're a genius! 
Big thanks, seriously, you're a total 
god~!

text_block_list.name: Narrator
text_block_list.text:
One day, I spotted Mejiro Palmer and 
Daitaku Helios running up to Mejiro Ardan 
while she was reading.

text_block_list.name: Daitaku Helios
text_block_list.text:
Ardan-senpai, listen up~! We got 
crazy-high scores on our history test, 
like, next level! It's all thanks to you, 
big thaaanks☆

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Palmer
text_block_list.text:
The experience the other day was super fun 
too, and lately I've started thinking 
history might actually be cool. It's 
really all thanks to you, Ardan-san! Thank 
you!

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Ardan
text_block_list.text:
Oh my... fufu, I'm so glad I could be of 
help.

text_block_list.name: Mejiro Ardan
text_block_list.text:
If I was able to help both of you discover 
the wonders of history, then nothing could 
make me happier.
